messages.task:
You are a meticulous financial-analysis assistant.  Below is the background narrative followed by the interface (tools) you can call to gather the numbers you need.  Think step-by-step, decide which tools help, call them as needed, perform any calculations in your scratch-pad, and then respond ONLY with the final numeric answer.

SCENARIO
Entergy Mississippi, Inc. – Management’s 2019 Financial Discussion and Analysis
• The company plans to spin off the utility’s transmission business (see the corresponding section of Entergy Corporation and Subsidiaries MDA for further details, including the planned retirement of debt and preferred securities).
• Results of operations
  – Net income 2011 compared to 2010: Net income increased $23.4 million primarily due to a lower effective income-tax rate.
  – Net income 2010 compared to 2009: Net income increased $6.0 million primarily due to higher net revenue and higher other income, partially offset by higher taxes other than income taxes, higher depreciation and amortisation expenses, and higher interest expense.
• Net revenue 2011 compared to 2010
  Net revenue consists of operating revenues net of (1) fuel, fuel-related expenses and gas purchased for resale, (2) purchased-power expenses and (3) other regulatory charges/credits.  An analysis of the change in net revenue comparing 2011 to 2010 is provided in the company’s internal bridge.
• Additional narrative highlights
  – The volume/weather variance is primarily due to a decrease of 97 GWh in weather-adjusted usage in the residential and commercial sectors and a decrease in sales volume in the unbilled-sales period.
  – The transmission-equalisation variance is primarily due to the addition in 2011 of transmission investments that are subject to equalisation.
  – Gross operating revenues increased primarily due to an increase of $57.5 million in gross wholesale revenues because of higher sales to affiliated customers, partially offset by a decrease of $26.9 million in power-management-rider revenue.
  – Fuel and purchased-power expenses increased primarily due to higher deferred fuel expense resulting from higher fuel revenues because of higher fuel rates, partially offset by a decrease in the average market prices of natural gas and purchased power.

TOOLS AVAILABLE
(All tools refer to the synthetic_finance.db database behind the scenes.)
1. list_items_by_category(category: str) -> List[str]
   Returns all line-item names within the given category (e.g. "net_revenue_variance", "expense", "gross_revenue", …).
2. get_amount_for_item_period(item_name: str, period: str) -> float
   Returns the numeric amount for the requested line item and comparison period (e.g. period "2011_vs_2010").
3. fetch_category_amounts(period: str, category: str) -> Dict[str, float]
   Returns a dictionary mapping every line-item in the chosen category to its amount for the specified period.
4. top_positive_variances(period: str, category: str, top_n: int = 3) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]
   Returns the largest positive variances (up to top_n) for quick inspection.
5. total_amount_for_category(period: str, category: str) -> float
   Returns the summed amount of all variances belonging to a category for a given period.

QUESTION
Based on the review of the net-revenue changes, what is the ratio of the volume/weather variance to the transmission-equalisation variance?

Remember: 1) You may call the tools multiple times; 2) show the final answer as a plain number with no explanation – it will be automatically verified.
